name: Scrape competitor YouTube channels for outlier videos with Bright Data, GPT-5.6, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Scrape competitor YouTube channels for the videos that beat their own baseline

Point it at a few competitor channels and it comes back with the videos that outperformed the channel that made them, each with the numbers that say so and a brief for your version.

### How it works
A weekly schedule sends one channel URL per competitor through Bright Data's YouTube discovery API. It takes a couple of minutes, so the workflow uses the asynchronous API properly: it triggers the scrape, then polls the snapshot on a Wait loop with a ten-minute cap until the rows are ready.

Every video is measured in views per day since it was published, then compared with the median views per day of that same channel, so a three year old video cannot win on age and a large channel cannot win on size. Shorts get their own baseline. A channel with fewer than four videos in the pool is skipped rather than compared against a median of one. GPT-5.6 reads the first minute of the transcript and the chapter titles and reports the structure: hook type, promise, topics.

Videos briefed recently are skipped for sixty days, the whole list lands in Google Sheets, and a ranked digest goes to Slack.

### Setup
Add a Bright Data API key as a Header Auth credential (`Authorization` / `Bearer YOUR_KEY`), connect OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack, then set your competitor channel URLs and channel name in Set Channel Config.

### Customization
Raise min_outlier_multiple for a shorter, stronger list, or set shorts_max_seconds to 0 to pool shorts and long form together.

## 1. Pick the channels
A few competitor channel URLs on a weekly schedule. Everything you would tune lives in one config node.

## 2. Scrape the channels asynchronously
Bright Data pulls the recent videos from each channel. It took over two minutes in testing, so this polls the snapshot until the rows are ready.

## 3. Compare each video to its own channel
Views per day against that channel's median, so age and channel size cannot decide the winner. Shorts get their own baseline.

## 4. Drop the ones you have had
The sheet doubles as the do-not-repeat list, so a video briefed recently stays out of this week's digest.

## 5. Read how the video is built
The model sees the first minute of the transcript and the chapter titles, and reports hook, promise and topics. Every number stated as fact comes from a field.

## 6. Deliver
One sheet row per outlier, which is what the next run reads back, plus a ranked Slack digest.

## Give each channel enough videos
The baseline is that channel's own median, so videos_per_channel below about ten leaves too few videos to build one from and the channel is skipped.
